title: A Windows drive is only half shut down
what: A Windows drive was not properly shut down (Fast Startup or hibernation), so Linux opens it read-only to protect it.
why: Writing to it from Linux could lose Windows files.
fix_summary: Open the Windows helper. It explains the safe way to switch Fast Startup off.
manual: In Windows, hold Shift and click Shut down. For good, switch off Fast Startup in Power Options.

title: A Windows drive is locked with BitLocker
what: A Windows drive is protected by BitLocker, so Linux cannot read it without the recovery key.
why: This is Windows' own encryption. Secure Linux never tries to bypass it.
fix_summary: Open the Windows helper to see how to unlock the drive with your key.

title: Windows keeps restarting by itself?
what: Windows is on this computer. If it restarts again and again, Linux cannot repair Windows itself, but can save your files.
why: Repeated restarts mean Windows' own start-up files are damaged. A Windows recovery USB can fix them.
fix_summary: Copy your Windows files to another drive first, then use Windows recovery.
manual: Boot a Windows install USB, choose Repair your computer, then Startup Repair.

title: Your Home Assistant server does not answer
what: The Home Assistant address you saved cannot be reached from here.
why: The server may be off, on another network, or the address changed.
fix_summary: Nothing to change on this computer.
manual: Check the server is on, and that you are on your home network or VPN.

title: Your Home Assistant key can be read by other users
what: The file with your Home Assistant access key can be read by other accounts on this computer.
why: Anyone with the key can control your home.
fix_summary: Make the key file private to the administrator.
undo: Run: sudo chmod 644 on the key file.
